A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAPS research and support reliable comparison of their text, equations, five figures and five tables. All ten pages of each were inspected. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both refer to supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, clustering, semantic-coherence and ablation results in Section 4 and Tables 1–5, including experiments on its self-collected industrial dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same motion tokenizer, latent-action energy, unsupervised threshold calibration, hysteresis controller, frozen Transformer embedding and cosine k-means clustering. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GTEA, Breakfast and the Industrial Motor Assembly dataset with top-down and exocentric views. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: ABD and OTAS in Table 1; Optical Flow, ABD and OTAS in Table 2; Attention-Norm Pooling in Table 3; and random pairs in Table 4. Newly cited Magma is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported protocols remain unchanged, including the two-hour annotated industrial test subset, F1@2s and F1@5s metrics, frozen Transformer configuration, and clustering evaluation on 6,444 segments with k = 3.

E4.justification: Both retain the same signal comparison, UMAP clustering analysis and Table 5 ablations examining quantization, motion representations and temporal embedding. No robustness test, case study or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains the same mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for ICSS. Neither version reports additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 4–5 are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains LAPS F1@2s scores of 81.27 and 81.93 for the two industrial views, and Table 4 retains overall ICSS of 0.926 ± 0.033.

T1.justification: The latent-action energy definition, threshold equations, normalized-distance identity and ICSS definition are unchanged. Visual inspection confirms that apparent mathematical differences in extracted text are extraction artifacts.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about unsupervised industrial action discovery, semantic segmentation and structured data for VLA pre-training. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of latent energy, quantization and temporal modeling remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitation to highly repetitive tasks and treats broader domains and robot task execution as future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page URL but removes the introduction's pledge to release code and the proprietary dataset upon acceptance, together with its supplementary-video notice. Section 4.1 still promises release of the annotated subset. Implementation details are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish actual resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Magma and contrasts its Trace-of-Mark supervision on pre-segmented clips with LAPS's segmentation of continuous streams. Other cited works are retained; changes to AgiBot authorship, the Moto publication entry and reference numbering concern bibliographic presentation.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the added Magma discussion, deleted release paragraph, project URL and bibliographic updates. The section order, terminology and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The added URL and text edits produce small layout shifts, including figure positioning and spacing around Table 5; References begins on page 8 instead of page 9. All five figures and five tables retain their content, captions and display structures.

improvement.justification: The added Magma comparison in Section 2 modestly improves research positioning by explaining the distinction from another tracking-based approach. Methods and experimental evidence are unchanged. The project URL provides an access pointer, but removal of the broader release pledge and unverified resource availability limit any claimed reproducibility benefit.
